## Problem

Found in PR #598 (#409), not yet on main.

The Check-side decorrelation note (`template/src/pdca_harness/leaves.py:3626-3631`, written from `_select_advisory` at `:3664`) is rebuilt on every Check: `:3644` deletes the previous one first. It is about that Check's own leaf selection ("confirm the review's independence by hand"), not about the patch. But it carries no leaf-status marker, so the #409 ledger treats it as an ordinary HUMAN finding and defers it into later rounds.

Example: round 1 has no `loop-telemetry.json`, so the note says the builder family is "unknown" and gets deferred. In round 2 the family is known and no note is written. The handover §6 still asks the human to confirm the independence of a review of a patch that was thrown away.

The plan-side twin (`_plan_decorrelation_note`, `:3827`) is not affected the same way: plan advisory is not re-run on iterate-do.

## Fix

Treat the Check decorrelation note like the stale/recovered infrastructure rows the #409 sign-off already exempts (`assemble.py:320-337` on the PR branch): do not defer it, and drop it once a later round no longer emits it.

## Done when

A decorrelation note from round N does not appear in round N+1's §6 when round N+1 wrote none. A test pins it.

Raised by the eduralph/pdca-pdca Act review of 2026-09-30 (issue_409 §6 row 4 / §10).
title: the Check decorrelation note is deferred like a finding, so it outlives the round it describes
